title: Security awareness training
intro: Read the information security and acceptable use policies, then answer these questions. You need 80% to pass; you can retake it.

questions.prompt: An email that looks like it is from a colleague asks you to sign in through a link to review a document. What do you do?
options: Sign in, since it is from a colleague
Check the sender and the link's real address, and if in doubt ask the colleague through another channel
Forward it to everyone to warn them
questions.correct: Check the sender and the link's real address, and if in doubt ask the colleague through another channel

questions.prompt: Where should multi-factor authentication be turned on?
options: Only on the email account
On every account that supports it
Only on accounts with admin rights
questions.correct: On every account that supports it

questions.prompt: Where may an API key for a production system be kept?
options: In the source code, if the repository is private
In a chat message to the person who needs it
In the approved secret store or password manager
questions.correct: In the approved secret store or password manager

questions.prompt: Your laptop is stolen. When do you report it?
options: Immediately, through the incident reporting channel
At the next team meeting
Only if it had customer data on it
questions.correct: Immediately, through the incident reporting channel

questions.prompt: May you paste customer data into an AI tool the company has not approved for that data?
options: Yes, if it helps you work faster
No
Yes, if you delete the conversation afterwards

questions.prompt: A teammate asks to borrow your login for a system they do not have access to. What do you do?
options: Share it for a few minutes
Decline, and point them to the access request process
Share it but change the password afterwards
questions.correct: Decline, and point them to the access request process

questions.prompt: Your operating system reports a security update. What do you do?
options: Install it promptly
Wait until something breaks
Turn off update notifications

questions.prompt: You notice unexpected admin activity in a production system. What is the first step?
options: Investigate quietly on your own
Report it through the incident reporting channel
Ignore it unless it happens again
questions.correct: Report it through the incident reporting channel

questions.prompt: Customer webhook payloads are which kind of information?
options: Public
Confidential, handled under the data classification policy
Internal but freely shareable
questions.correct: Confidential, handled under the data classification policy

questions.prompt: What should happen when you step away from your computer?
options: Nothing, if the office is safe
Lock the screen
Close the browser
